g.text: How well do AI-image detectors generalize
when generators, presentation, and manipulation change?
Shriya Rajesh • Jeslyn Yang • Aditya Lanjewar • Jad Barmada • Saisha Hongal • Medini Patil • Rachel Lin | USC CSCI 566
More generator types at the same image
Detectors that perform well on generated
images can fail differently on face crops.
Eight unseen generators × four diversity levels ×
three dataset repeats × two training modes.
1,400 real + 1,400 fake images per training run.
ResNet-50 fine-tuned vs frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 + head.
Equal-weight holdouts; 18 GPT invalid fakes omitted.
Pipelines differ in architecture and pretraining.
JPEG60: fewer false alarms, more missed fakes.
All 8 holdouts; k=7. ViT AUROC ≈ 0.85 in both.
VLMs flag 0/70 reals in all views. 40 sources
excluded for at least one invalid GPT score.
CNN flags 53/54 real crops; GPT detects 16/135
fakes. Balanced accuracy is ~50% for both.
ViT and Claude also falsely flag 42/54 reals.
Identity and mirror labels remain unverified; adapted
head trained on three methods (prior test inspection).
Generalization is conditional: report the test domain, image preparation, and both class error rates.

Context: GenImage (Zhu et al., 2023); Community Forensics (Park & Owens, 2025); Fake or JPEG? (Grommelt et al., 2024); DF40 (Yan et al., 2024). • Results & reproducibility: github.com/JBarmada/CSCI566-AI-Image-Classifier
